entities.summary: Michael J. Gibbons was an American boxer from 1908 to 1922. The brother of heavyweight Tommy Gibbons, he claimed Middleweight Champion of the World status in 1909 following Stanley Ketchel's murder. Although he never won the title, Gibbons is regarded as one of the all-time best welter and middleweight boxers by historians. Statistical boxing website BoxRec lists Gibbons as the #18 ranked middleweight of all time, while The Ring Magazine founder Nat Fleischer placed him at #9. The International Boxing Research Organization rates Gibbons as the 17th best middleweight ever and boxing historian Bert Sugar placed him 92nd in his Top 100 Fighters catalogue.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Gibbons' claim to Middleweight Champion of the World status in 1909 led to a brief period of uncertainty in the boxing world, with some considering him the true champion. His ranking among the all-time best welter and middleweight boxers reflects his enduring legacy as one of the greatest pound-for-pound fighters in history.
